extracted.intended_audience: journalists, public relations professionals, and the general public (readers of organizational press releases)
extracted.subtask_description: A short organizational press release reporting the election of a new president and other officers, providing quotes, background statistics, and related organizational news. Serves as an example/template for election/leadership announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear headline announcing the main news
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise headline that states the principal news item (who was elected and to what office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from page: 'PRSA ASSEMBLY ELECTS WOLCOTT AS PRESIDENT' — headline immediately conveys the event and subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph stating who, what, when, where
rubrics_metrics.description: The opening paragraph should state the person's full name, current title/affiliation, the office to which they were elected, the organization, and the meeting/date/location context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example wording: 'Robert B. Wolcott, Jr., president, Robert B. Wolcott Associates, Inc., Los Angeles, was elected 1966 president of the Public Relations Society of America at the annual meeting of the Society's Assembly of Delegates held in New York City, Saturday (Nov. 20).' — this packs name, title, affiliation, office, organization, meeting and date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify who announced or reported the action (e.g., outgoing president, chair, or official spokesman).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Mr. Wolcott's election ... was announced by 1965 president, Ovid R. Davis, vice-president of the Coca-Cola Co., Atlanta.' — provides source/authority for the news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include direct quotation of principal's plans or comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide at least one direct quote from the elected individual summarizing intent, priorities, or a notable statement about their upcoming term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example quote used: 'We should articulate all sides of a major public issue,' and Wolcott's stated plan to "activate the PRSA in support of important public questions dealing with social, economic and moral issues." Quotes personalize the announcement and state priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name and explain any new program or initiative (with acronym if used)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the principal announces a program or initiative, include its name, purpose, and any explanation of its naming or acronym.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'The name for this effort will be Program for Responsible Service to America (taken from the initials of the PR society.)' — gives name and rationale for acronym.

rubrics_metrics.name: List additional officers with titles and affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the names, official titles, and organizational affiliations of other officers elected or re-elected (vice-presidents, secretary, treasurer, directors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example entries: 'J. Carroll Bateman, general manager, Insurance Information Institute, New York, vice-president; James G. Shea, general public relations manager, Southern Pacific Company, San Francisco, secretary; John H. Sattler ... was re-elected treasurer.' — full ID of individuals and roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report organizational statistics and membership context
rubrics_metrics.description: Include relevant organization metrics (membership size, accreditation numbers, application/acceptance statistics) to give context to the significance of the announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'head the 5,100 member organization'; 'a preliminary list ... of 430 public relations men who have been accredited'; and reporting that '19 applicants were turned down this year' with breakdowns by chapter/national/board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe policy or governance actions affecting membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize any committee findings, policy changes, or governance decisions that affect membership standards or selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'The PRSA National Eligibility Committee reported moves whereby the Society will be more selective in granting membership... "As public relations continues to grow in professionalism, we must strive to be more selective," it was stated.' — describes the committee's intent and evidence (rejection numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose key financial information when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: When financially relevant, provide concise financial figures (e.g., receipts, budget status) to inform stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'the Society's financial status at the end of October showed total gross receipts of $393,270.' — a single clear financial data point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announce related organizations' leadership or foundation news
rubrics_metrics.description: If affiliated foundations or related bodies have news (elections, appointments), include their leadership results and titles to present the broader institutional picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Glen Perry ... was elected as president of the Foundation for Public Relations Research and Education. Ward B. Stevenson ... was chosen Foundation vice-president.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use full professional titles and institutional affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistently attach professional titles and employer/institution for all named individuals to establish credibility and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples through the release: each person is followed by role and company/university/city (e.g., 'Glen Perry, director of public relations, E. I. du Pont de Nemours & Co., Inc., Wilmington').

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide background/context to explain significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Include historical, programmatic, or policy background (e.g., accreditation program started this year) so readers understand why the news matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'a preliminary list ... of 430 public relations men who have been accredited under the Society's professional accreditation program which began this year.' — situates the accreditation figure in program timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and timing clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the city and precise date (or meeting day) to anchor the event in time and place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example phrasing: 'at the annual meeting of the Society's Assembly of Delegates held in New York City, Saturday (Nov. 20).' — specifies location and date of the meeting.
